newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to rely more on foreign borrowing in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to rely more on foreign borrowing in 1997.

text.p: Turkey will rely more on foreign borrowing next year to lower high domestic interest rates, State Minister Ufuk Soylemez said on Wednesday.
"Our target is to extend the maturity of domestic borrowing and to go for foreign debts as much as possible," Soylemez told reporters.

The Turkish Treasury set an annual compound interest rate of 144.92 percent on its six-month bills auctioned last week, including a 10 percent witholding tax to be charged from interest income in 1997.
"We should at least roll over our foreign debt servicing next year," Soylemez said.

Turkey raised some $3 billion from international debt markets this year and $2 billion from domestic banks through the sale of foreign currency-denominated bonds, against its foreign debt service of $7.5 billion, Soylemez said.
Annual inflation runs at around 80 percent.
